qa.overall_assessment: BA spec is implementable, falsifiable, and free of meaningful scope drift. Five ACs are concrete, each names specific files+line ranges, each has a deterministic grep/Read acceptance test. Origin trace for AC-WID5 is FULLY VERIFIED — `efca767` HEAD-committed `posttool-subagent-track.py` has no `contract is None` block (its `sys.exit(0)` calls are at lines 92/119/128, all under `if not stdin_data`/`if state is None`/`if ip_index is None`/etc gates, NOT under any `contract is None` gate); the current working tree shows file as modified (M) per `git status`; `hooks/lib/contract_runtime.py` is untracked (not in `git ls-files hooks/lib/`). The proposed fall-through fix RESTORES the legacy `record_subagent_call()` behaviour that existed in `efca767` and was deleted by the working-tree refactor — this is a regression repair, not a new design. Overnight strictness is preserved because the contract-runtime path is only entered when contract is non-None, which only `/dev-overnight` produces. Six advisory objections recorded; zero blockers. Spec is ready for dev with one optional polish edit to AC-WID3 wording (orchestrator's prompt mislabels §5.3 as 'Section 6'; BA correctly edits §5.3 but inherits the mislabel).

objections.description: BA spec inherits orchestrator-prompt mislabel 'Section 6 Out-of-Scope text' but the saga's actual `## Section 6` is `## Section 6: Why Not Met` (line 477), NOT Out-of-Scope. The actual Out-of-Scope subsection is `### 5.3: Out of scope (won't have)` at line 453 (which is part of Section 5). BA's edit target (§5.3 between lines 457 and 459) is CORRECT — /close Bullet 3 evaluates against §5.3 per the close-report's own wording at line 25 ('Saga spec §5.3 Out of Scope (lines 453–457)'). The AC title and several body references still say 'Section 6' which is technically wrong but harmless (every reader who reads the close-report Bullet 3 evidence will route to §5.3 anyway). Optional spec polish: rename AC-WID3 to 'Saga §5.3 documents AC12 literal-E2E as on-site-unreachable goal' and remove 'Section 6' from the AC body.
objections.suggested_fix: Optional: replace the three 'Section 6' / '§6' phrases in AC-WID3 (BA spec lines 19-20, 51-52, and the title) with '§5.3' so the AC label matches the actual edit site. Not a blocker — the dev edit-site is unambiguous.

objections.description: AC-WID1d says `dev.files_modified` and `dev.files_created` MUST be 'required top-level lists at the dev root' but the test phrasing in BA spec lines 549-557 says only 'appear as required top-level keys at the dev root (not only inside per-task tasks_completed[])'. There is no concrete grep test that distinguishes 'required' from 'illustrated as one possible field'. A dev edit that adds an example block showing `"files_modified": []` at the dev root WITHOUT adding language that says 'these fields MUST be present at the dev root' would technically satisfy the grep but not the spirit. The fix is small: state explicitly that dev-report consumers (commit.sh) require these at dev root, and the test should be 'grep -E "dev\.files_modified.*MUST|required at dev root" /root/.claude/agents/dev.md returns ≥1 match'.
objections.suggested_fix: Strengthen AC-WID1d test condition to require literal phrase 'MUST be non-null lists at the dev root' (or equivalent) in dev.md output template prose, in addition to the example block showing them at the dev root.

objections.description: AC-WID2 grep test (BA spec lines 561-567) requires 'No prefixed forms.*permitted in NEW artifacts' to appear in all five files. The 5th location is `/root/.claude/commands/dev.md` (completion-report template region). The grep is correct but the BA spec is silent on which line of `commands/dev.md` the convention paragraph should land — line 982-1014 (JSON Storage Policy region) is suggested at line 654 (Technical Hints) but not bound to the AC. Dev could place it anywhere in `commands/dev.md` and pass the grep. Recommend pinning the placement to a specific line region (e.g. immediately after the completion-report template at line 980).
objections.suggested_fix: Add a placement constraint to AC-WID2: 'in `/root/.claude/commands/dev.md`, the convention paragraph MUST land between line 980 (end of completion-report template) and line 1020 (JSON Storage Policy boundary)'.

objections.description: Fix direction is sound (verified: efca767's original `record_subagent_call()` did exactly this) but BA spec's Notes/Provenance section says 'a HARD-CUTOVER silent passthrough comment that intentionally bypasses /dev/redev cycles, but the validator (pretool-todo-validate.py) was not updated to match. This is a half-applied refactor.' The half-applied refactor diagnosis is correct, but the proposed fix only repairs the writer side. There is a latent question: did the refactor author INTEND for `/dev` and `/redev` cycles to also start using cycle-contract.json (i.e. the 'right' fix is to make `/dev`/`/redev` produce a contract, not to fall-through)? The answer is implied by NS-6 (overnight-strictness preserved) and by the fact that `commands/dev.md` does not currently produce a cycle-contract — but BA spec does not address this design question explicitly. Recommend a one-line note clarifying the design choice: 'The fall-through is permanent, not a stopgap; /dev and /redev will not adopt cycle-contract.json'.
objections.suggested_fix: Add a one-line clarification to AC-WID5 root-cause section: 'The fall-through path is the long-term design for /dev and /redev cycles; only /dev-overnight produces and consumes cycle-contract.json'.

objections.description: BA spec says 'lines 192-194' (BA spec line 596) and 'lines 193-194' (BA spec line 620) interchangeably. Read of `posttool-subagent-track.py` confirms the actual `if contract is None: sys.exit(0)` is at lines 193-194 (line 192 is the contract load itself, which must be PRESERVED so overnight cycles still validate). Dev should NOT delete line 192. Recommend tightening the wording in BA spec lines 596-602 and 619-630 to consistently say 'replace the body of the `if contract is None:` block at lines 193-194' — preserving line 192 (`contract = contract_runtime.load_contract(session_id, cycle_id)`) explicitly.
objections.suggested_fix: Normalize all line-range references in AC-WID5 to '193-194 (the `sys.exit(0)` body of the `if contract is None:` block)'; preserve line 192 (the `contract_runtime.load_contract()` call).

objections.description: BA spec line 168 quote of close.md Bullet 4 verbatim verified (matches actual line 168). The proposed two-clause Bullet 4 rewording risks ambiguity if dev fails to PRESERVE existing FAIL semantics for the OTHER failure modes Bullet 4 currently catches (manual `git commit` outside agent context, auto-bulk-pattern bypass, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR override). The orchestrator's prompt says 'any sub-item requiring user-only physical filesystem actions is N/A-with-reason, NOT FAIL' — but commit-bypass via auto-bulk pattern is also a 'human bypass' and might confusingly read as also N/A. Recommend explicit listing in AC-WID4 of the failure modes that MUST stay as FAIL (manual git commit outside agent context, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR override, auto-bulk-pattern abuse) so dev does not accidentally widen the N/A clause.
objections.suggested_fix: Add to AC-WID4 acceptance test: 'AND the bullet text retains FAIL classification for: (i) manual git commit outside agent context, (ii) CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR override, (iii) auto-bulk-pattern bypass abuse. Only the .hook-refactor-allow sentinel touch (and structurally-equivalent user-only physical filesystem actions) becomes N/A-with-reason.'

origin_trace_verification.conclusion: BA's origin-trace claim is fully accurate. The fix-direction (fall-through legacy bookkeeping when contract is None) is regression-repair of working-tree-only damage.

safety.rationale: The fix only modifies the `contract is None` branch. The contract-runtime path (line 198: _enforce) is unreached when contract is None, so the fix's added code cannot interact with it. Line 192 (contract load) is preserved. There is no shared state between the legacy bookkeeping write and the contract-runtime validate.

overnight_compat.rationale: When /dev-overnight produces cycle-contract.json, contract_runtime.load_contract() returns non-None, and the new fall-through branch is skipped entirely. Overnight strictness (NS-6) is preserved by construction. Verified by reading lines 192-198 of current posttool-subagent-track.py: the contract-non-None path goes to _enforce(stdin_data, contract, state, bm_path, step) which is unaffected by AC-WID5.

simplicity.rationale: The legacy bookkeeping function `record_subagent_call(state, ip_index, bm_path)` already exists in efca767's source — dev can copy its body verbatim into the contract-is-None branch. ~8-12 lines, no new abstractions, no new dependencies. The risk is purely 'did dev copy the right lines' which is grep-verifiable.

hidden_couplings.rationale: Searched for hidden couplings: (a) pretool-subagent-enforce.py reads subagent_calls but its read is gated by canonical step's subagent_call schema, same as today; (b) the bookmark file's other fields (last_todos, cycle_id, command) are not touched by the fall-through write; (c) no concurrent-write hazard because the hook is single-process per Agent invocation. One subtle issue: the original `record_subagent_call()` does fresh-read-then-write (re-loads the bookmark via `bm_path.read_text()` to avoid stale state), which the BA spec doesn't explicitly call out. Dev should preserve this fresh-read-then-write semantic, not write to the in-memory `state` dict that may be stale. Recommend dev copy the original record_subagent_call body verbatim.
